title: The night Coventry burned

facts.text: On the night of 14 November 1940, 515 German bombers attacked the English industrial city of Coventry in a raid code named Moonlight Sonata.
The first marker flares fell at 19:20, and the all clear did not sound until 06:15 the next morning, about ten hours later.
The bombers dropped about 500 tonnes of high explosives, including 50 parachute mines, and about 36,000 incendiary bombs.
An estimated 568 people were killed, though the exact figure was never confirmed, and more than 1,200 were injured.
More than 4,300 homes were destroyed, and about two thirds of the city's buildings were damaged.
The medieval Cathedral of St Michael caught fire around 8 p.m. and burned to a shell. Its ruins still stand beside the new cathedral.
In the ruins, stonemason Jock Forbes found two charred roof beams that had fallen in the shape of a cross, bound them together, and set them on an altar of rubble.
The cathedral's provost, Richard Howard, had the words 'Father Forgive' put on the wall behind the altar of the ruined church.
German propaganda turned the city's name into a verb, 'coventrieren', meaning to wipe out a city from the air.

sources.title: Coventry Cathedral, Father Forgive, Liberation Route Europe

photoNote: The centre of Coventry the morning after the raid of 14 to 15 November 1940: smoking rubble, firemen hosing ruins, a bus and the gutted Owen Owen store. Ministry of Information official photo, Imperial War Museum H 5600, Crown copyright expired, public domain (via Wikimedia Commons, 1920 px). Not the cathedral; a war artist drawing of the cathedral ruins (Randolph Schwabe, IWM Art 22482) exists but is a drawing, not a photo.
photoCredit: The centre of Coventry after the German air raid of 14 November 1940. Imperial War Museum H 5600, public domain.

declassified.fact: Provost Howard also made a cross from medieval nails found in the ruins. Copies of that Cross of Nails have since been given to churches and groups around the world, which formed the Community of the Cross of Nails in 1974.

sources.title: The Cross of Nails Society, h2g2

body:
In the ruins of the cathedral, a stonemason found two charred roof beams that had fallen in the shape of a cross.

14 November 1940. That night, 515 German bombers attacked the English industrial city of Coventry. The first marker flares fell at 19:20, and the all clear did not sound until 06:15 the next morning.

An estimated 568 people were killed, though the exact figure was never confirmed. More than 4,300 homes were destroyed, and the medieval Cathedral of St Michael burned to a shell.

Jock Forbes bound the beams together and set them on an altar of rubble. The provost, Richard Howard, had two words put on the wall behind it: "Father Forgive."
